Handle missing and low-coverage observations explicitly

Source: R/gapfill.R
ntl_gapfill.Rd

Applies one documented rule to the missing cells of an ntl_panel(), and flags unit-months at risk of summer stray-light gaps. VIIRS cannot observe at night when the sun barely sets, so units north of about 45 degrees have missing or contaminated values around the June solstice (in northern Kazakhstan typically May to August). Silently averaging whatever pixels remain creates spurious seasonal swings; this function makes the choice visible.

Usage

ntl_gapfill(
  panel,
  rule = c("interp", "seasonal", "drop", "none"),
  max_gap = 2,
  units = NULL,
  lat_threshold = NULL,
  months = 5:8
)

Arguments

panel

An ntl_panel.

rule

One of "interp", "seasonal", "drop", "none".

max_gap

Longest run of missing periods to interpolate (rule = "interp").

units

Optional unit polygons (with the panel's id column), used with lat_threshold to flag stray-light risk.

lat_threshold

Latitude (degrees north) from which units are flagged during months. A unit's latitude is that of a point on its surface.

months

Calendar months flagged as stray-light risk.

Value

The panel with columns imputed, impute_method and, if units and lat_threshold are given, lat and stray_light_risk. The attribute gap_report counts missing cells by month before and after filling.

Details

Rules:

  • "none": only add flags.

  • "drop": remove missing rows (the panel becomes unbalanced).

  • "interp": linear interpolation within each unit for interior runs of at most max_gap missing periods.

  • "seasonal" (monthly panels): multiplicative fill value = S[unit, month] * L[unit, year], where S is the unit's seasonal index (median ratio of a month to the deseasonalised annual level) and L is the unit's deseasonalised level in that year. A calendar month that is never observed for a unit cannot be filled and stays NA; consider annual data or dropping those months.

Filled values are marked with imputed = TRUE and impute_method, so you can run robustness checks with and without them.

Examples

ex <- ntl_example()
m <- ntl_files(ex$dir, "eog_vnl_monthly")
m <- m[m$series == "eog_vnl_monthly_npp" &
         m$period < as.Date("2022-01-01"), ]
long <- ntl_extract(m, ex$units_old, id_col = "district", quiet = TRUE)
p <- ntl_panel(long, min_share_valid = 0.5)
p2 <- ntl_gapfill(p,
  rule = "interp", max_gap = 2,
  units = ex$units_old, lat_threshold = 48
)
attr(p2, "gap_report")
#>    month missing_before missing_after
#> 1      1              0             0
#> 2      2              0             0
#> 3      3              0             0
#> 4      4              0             0
#> 5      5              0             0
#> 6      6              3             0
#> 7      7              3             0
#> 8      8              0             0
#> 9      9              0             0
#> 10    10              0             0
#> 11    11              0             0
#> 12    12              0             0
